Name: Fingolimod
Paper Title: Fingolimod in children with Rett syndrome: the FINGORETT study
Note: Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator evaluated in the FINGORETT clinical study in girls with Rett syndrome to reduce neuroinflammation and improve neurological function.

Name: Levodopa
Paper Title: Improvement of the Rett syndrome phenotype in a MeCP2 mouse model upon treatment with levodopa and a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor
Note: Dopamine precursor used together with a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor; improved phenotype in MeCP2-mutant mice with effects on motor function and the dopaminergic system.

Name: Tyrosine
Paper Title: Biochemical and clinical effects of tyrosine and tryptophan in the Rett syndrome
Note: Catecholamine precursor amino acid; studied in RTT for its biochemical effects on dopamine and serotonin metabolism in combination with tryptophan.

Name: Triheptanoin
Paper Title: Anaplerotic triheptanoin diet enhances mitochondrial substrate use to remodel the metabolome and improve lifespan, motor function, and sociability in MeCP2-null mice
Note: Anaplerotic 7-carbon medium-chain triglyceride; improved mitochondrial function and lifespan in Mecp2-null mice by remodeling the brain metabolome.

Name: Trolox
Paper Title: Systemic Radical Scavenger Treatment of a Mouse Model of Rett Syndrome: Merits and Limitations of the Vitamin E Derivative Trolox
Note: Water-soluble vitamin E analogue with antioxidant activity; evaluated in RTT mice to reduce oxidative stress; showed partial benefits with long-term limitations.

Name: Midazolam
Paper Title: The benzodiazepine Midazolam mitigates the breathing defects of Mecp2-deficient mice
Note: Short-acting benzodiazepine; mitigated breathing defects in Mecp2-deficient mice by acting on GABA-A receptors in respiratory brainstem centers.

Name: Melatonin
Paper Title: Management of sleep disorders in children with neurodevelopmental disorders: A review
Note: Neuroendocrine hormone with antioxidant properties; used in RTT for management of sleep disorders common in the syndrome; reviewed as part of pharmacological strategies in neurodevelopmental disorders.

Name: Diazepam
Paper Title: A case-controlled comparison of postoperative analgesic dosing between girls with Rett syndrome and girls with and without developmental disability undergoing spinal fusion surgery
Note: GABA-A agonist benzodiazepine; studied in the context of postoperative pain management in girls with RTT undergoing spinal fusion surgery; useful for spasm and anxiety control.

Name: Clenbuterol
Paper Title: Neurodevelopmental disorders: Righting Rett syndrome with IGF1
Note: Beta-2 adrenergic agonist that stimulates IGF-1 production; proposed as a therapeutic strategy for RTT based on the IGF-1/PI3K signaling pathway.

Name: Fluoxetine
Paper Title: Fluoxetine increases brain MeCP2 immuno-positive cells in a female Mecp2 heterozygous mouse model of Rett syndrome through endogenous serotonin
Note: SSRI that increased MeCP2 immunopositive cells in heterozygous Mecp2 mice via endogenous serotonin; also rescued motor deficits in a heterozygous RTT mouse model.

Name: Valproic acid
Paper Title: SAMe, choline, and valproic acid as possible epigenetic drugs: Their effects in pregnancy with a special emphasis on animal studies
Note: Antiepileptic drug with epigenetic properties (HDAC inhibitor); reviewed as an epigenetic agent with potential modulatory effect in RTT; also documented as a teratogen with a relevant risk profile.

Name: CX546
Paper Title: The enhancement of activity rescues the establishment of Mecp2 null neuronal phenotypes
Note: Positive allosteric modulator of AMPA receptors (ampakine); rescued neuronal phenotypes in Mecp2-null cells by enhancing glutamatergic synaptic activity and neuronal plasticity.

Name: Carbamazepine
Paper Title: Antiepileptic drugs in Rett syndrome
Note: Sodium channel-blocking antiepileptic drug; documented in clinical use in RTT patients for seizure control; reviewed in a European multicenter study on antiepileptic drugs in RTT.

Name: Curcumin
Paper Title: Vascular dysfunction in a mouse model of Rett syndrome and effects of curcumin treatment
Note: Natural polyphenol with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; corrected vascular dysfunction in a Mecp2-deficient RTT mouse model by improving vasodilatory responses.

Name: Tianeptine
Paper Title: Drug repurposing in Rett and Rett-like syndromes: A promising yet underrated opportunity?
Note: Atypical antidepressant modulating glutamate and serotonin; reviewed as a drug repurposing candidate for RTT and Rett-like syndromes.

Name: Allopregnanolone
Paper Title: Time-dependent modulation of GABAA-ergic synaptic transmission by allopregnanolone in locus coeruleus neurons of Mecp2-null mice
Note: Endogenous neurosteroid and positive modulator of GABA-A receptors; time-dependently modulated GABAergic transmission in locus coeruleus neurons of Mecp2-null mice.

Name: Clonidine
Paper Title: Management of self-injurious behaviors in children with neurodevelopmental disorders: A pharmacotherapy overview
Note: Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist; reviewed for management of self-injurious behaviors and hyperactivity in neurodevelopmental disorders including RTT.

Name: Desipramine
Paper Title: Effect of desipramine on patients with breathing disorders in Rett syndrome
Note: Tricyclic antidepressant (norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor); demonstrated improvement of breathing disorders in RTT patients in a clinical trial specifically targeting apneas and hyperpneas.

Name: Donepezil
Paper Title: Mecp2 deletion from cholinergic neurons selectively impairs recognition memory and disrupts cholinergic modulation of the perirhinal cortex
Note: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; Mecp2 deletion in cholinergic neurons selectively impaired recognition memory and cholinergic modulation; Donepezil proposed to correct this deficit.

Name: Lamotrigine
Paper Title: Lamotrigine in two cases of Rett syndrome
Note: Membrane-stabilizing antiepileptic drug; reported in two RTT clinical cases with seizure improvement; blocks sodium channels and modulates glutamate release.

Name: Trazodone
Paper Title: Drug repurposing in Rett and Rett-like syndromes: A promising yet underrated opportunity?
Note: Serotonin reuptake inhibitor and 5-HT2 antagonist antidepressant; reviewed as a repurposing candidate for RTT in the context of mood and sleep symptoms.

Name: Mirtazapine
Paper Title: Mirtazapine treatment in a young female mouse model of Rett syndrome identifies time windows for the rescue of early phenotypes
Note: Noradrenergic and serotonergic antidepressant; identified critical time windows for rescue of early phenotypes in a young RTT mouse model; effective before full symptom onset.

Name: Glutamic acid
Paper Title: RIPK1 activation in Mecp2-deficient microglia promotes inflammation and glutamate release in RTT
Note: Excitatory neurotransmitter; RIPK1 activation in Mecp2-deficient microglia was shown to promote inflammation and excessive glutamate release in RTT pointing to the glutamatergic system as a therapeutic target.

Name: Trofinetide
Paper Title: Trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome: A randomized phase 3 study
Note: Synthetic IGF-1 analogue; FDA-approved in 2023 (Daybue) for RTT in patients aged 2 and older; demonstrated improvement in behavioral symptoms and global function in a phase 3 clinical trial.

Name: Lovastatin
Paper Title: Lovastatin fails to improve motor performance and survival in methyl-CpG-binding protein2-null mice
Note: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin); failed to improve motor performance and survival in Mecp2-null mice despite proposed neuroprotective mechanisms.

Name: Citalopram
Paper Title: Fluoxetine rescues rotarod motor deficits in Mecp2 heterozygous mouse model of Rett syndrome via brain serotonin
Note: SSRI reviewed in the context of serotonergic modulation in RTT; both citalopram and fluoxetine act on the serotonergic system which is disrupted in heterozygous Mecp2 mouse models.

Name: Blarcamesine
Paper Title: The new big is small: Leveraging knowledge from small trials for rare disease drug development: Blarcamesine for Rett syndrome
Note: Sigma-1 receptor agonist; evaluated in a clinical trial for RTT; a methodological study addressed how to leverage data from small trials for rare disease drug development.

Name: Lysine
Paper Title: Role of H3K4 demethylases in complex neurodevelopmental diseases
Note: Essential amino acid with a role in post-translational histone modifications (H3K4 methylation); reviewed in the epigenetic context of complex neurodevelopmental diseases including RTT.

Name: Vigabatrin
Paper Title: Epileptic spasms in CDKL5 deficiency disorder: Delayed treatment and poor response to first-line therapies
Note: Irreversible GABA-transaminase inhibitor antiepileptic; documented in epileptic spasms in CDKL5 deficiency disorder (RTT-related); variable response to first-line therapies reported.

Name: Cannabidiol
Paper Title: Cannabidiol therapy for refractory epilepsy and seizure disorders
Note: Non-psychoactive cannabinoid with antiepileptic activity; reviewed for refractory epilepsy and seizure disorders; proposed as an alternative for RTT patients with treatment-resistant epilepsy.

Name: Gentamicin
Paper Title: Evaluation of novel enhancer compounds in gentamicin-mediated readthrough of nonsense mutations in Rett syndrome
Note: Aminoglycoside with nonsense mutation readthrough capacity; evaluated as an enhancer of functional MeCP2 protein production in MECP2 mutations that generate premature stop codons.

Name: Naltrexone
Paper Title: Rett syndrome: Controlled study of an oral opiate antagonist, naltrexone
Note: Opioid receptor antagonist; evaluated in a controlled trial in RTT; showed modest effects on breathing and behavior that were not sustained over time.

Name: 7,8-Dihydroxyflavone
Paper Title: From cannabinoids and neurosteroids to statins and the ketogenic diet: New therapeutic avenues in Rett syndrome?
Note: TrkB receptor agonist (BDNF receptor); reviewed as a neuroprotective candidate in RTT for its ability to mimic BDNF signaling without requiring the protein itself.

Name: Memantine
Paper Title: Is memantine a potential therapeutic for Rett syndrome?
Note: Non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist; proposed as therapy for RTT given the excitatory/inhibitory imbalance; systematic review of preclinical evidence.

Name: LM22A-4
Paper Title: A small-molecule TrkB ligand improves dendritic spine phenotypes and atypical behaviors in female Rett syndrome mice
Note: Small TrkB ligand (BDNF receptor); improved dendritic spine morphology and atypical behaviors in female RTT mice; promising preclinical results from a preprint study.

Name: Cannabivarin
Paper Title: From cannabinoids and neurosteroids to statins and the ketogenic diet: New therapeutic avenues in Rett syndrome?
Note: Phytocannabinoid analogue of cannabidiol with a shorter side chain; reviewed among cannabinoids and neurosteroids as possible therapeutic strategies in RTT.

Name: Benserazide
Paper Title: Altered trajectories of neurodevelopment and behavior in mouse models of Rett syndrome
Note: Peripheral dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor; combined with levodopa to increase central dopamine availability; evaluated in a RTT mouse model improving neurodevelopmental trajectories and behavior.

Name: Dextromethorphan
Paper Title: Randomized open-label trial of dextromethorphan in Rett syndrome
Note: NMDA antagonist and sigma-1 agonist; evaluated in a randomized open-label clinical trial in RTT; showed trends of improvement in some behavioral symptoms without strong statistical significance.

Name: Alanine
Paper Title: Treating Rett syndrome: From mouse models to human therapies
Note: Non-essential amino acid; reviewed within metabolic and nutritional strategies in RTT; role in the glucose-alanine cycle relevant to neuronal energy metabolism.

Name: Risperidone
Paper Title: Modulation of serotonin receptors in neurodevelopmental disorders: Focus on 5-HT7 receptor
Note: Atypical antipsychotic D2 and 5-HT2 antagonist; reviewed for modulation of serotonin receptors (especially 5-HT7) in neurodevelopmental disorders such as RTT; used for behavioral symptom management.

Name: Folic acid
Paper Title: Cerebral folate deficiency
Note: Vitamin B9; reviewed in the context of cerebral folate deficiency that can coexist with RTT; involved in neurotransmitter synthesis and DNA methylation.

Name: Vatiquinone
Paper Title: Profile of Trofinetide in the treatment of Rett syndrome: Design, development and potential place in therapy
Note: Vitamin E analogue with mitochondrial antioxidant activity (15-LOX inhibitor); reviewed in the context of neuroprotection strategies in RTT alongside trofinetide.

Name: Cysteamine
Paper Title: Unexpected link between Huntington disease and Rett syndrome
Note: Aminothiol with neuroprotective properties; identified through an unexpected link between Huntington disease and RTT; acts by elevating BDNF levels and reducing protein aggregate accumulation.

Name: Picrotoxinin
Paper Title: GABAA receptor antagonism ameliorates behavioral and synaptic impairments associated with MeCP2 overexpression
Note: Active component of picrotoxin; GABA-A receptor antagonist (chloride channel blocker); GABA-A antagonism ameliorated behavioral and synaptic impairments in mice overexpressing MeCP2.

Name: Sarizotan
Paper Title: Potent hERG channel inhibition by sarizotan, an investigative treatment for Rett syndrome
Note: 5-HT1A agonist and partial D2 agonist; investigated for RTT to manage apneas; identified as a potent hERG channel inhibitor representing an important cardiac safety signal.

Name: Bromocriptine
Paper Title: Bromocriptine in the Rett syndrome
Note: D2 dopaminergic agonist; one of the earliest drugs evaluated in RTT; early clinical study explored its effect on the dopaminergic dysfunction observed in the syndrome.

Name: Picrotin
Paper Title: GABAA receptor antagonism ameliorates behavioral and synaptic impairments associated with MeCP2 overexpression
Note: Inactive component of picrotoxin with a structure analogous to picrotoxinin; included as a structural reference; the study jointly evaluated GABA-A antagonism in the context of MeCP2 overexpression.
